documents.description: The classes and Harmony patches of the Bitshifter mod (src/Bitshifter): entry point and compatibility checks, 31-bit depth, display, side screen, NOT gate and overlay label guard, with locations and rules

sections.heading: BitshifterMod
sections.title: BitshifterMod
sections.description: The `UserMod2` entry point. Applies the patches in `OnAllModsLoaded` (not `OnLoad`) so the compatibility check sees every other mod's patches, and stands down when another mod already widens the reader or writer.

sections.heading: Reader and Writer bit depth
sections.title: Reader and Writer bit depth
sections.description: `LogicRibbonReader.GetBitDepth` and `LogicRibbonWriter.GetBitDepth` are postfixed to return `Bits`. The bit selector side screen builds one row per `GetBitDepth()`, and both buildings already shift by the selected bit with no upper bound, so this is the whole functional change.

sections.heading: Display
sections.title: Display
sections.description: Shared draw code for both buildings. Replaces the vanilla four bit lights with a two-digit seven-segment display of the selected bit (1-based) and one light for that bit's state.

sections.heading: LogicBitSelectorSideScreen scroll view
sections.title: LogicBitSelectorSideScreen scroll view
sections.description: A postfix on `LogicBitSelectorSideScreen.SetTarget` wraps the rows' container in a `KScrollRect` (with `RectMask2D`, `LayoutElement` and `ContentSizeFitter`) the first time the screen is shown. The viewport is 1.5 times the height of the vanilla four rows, with a permanent scrollbar cloned from a vanilla side screen (a flat-colour bar is the fallback). The same postfix clamps layout widths to the details panel header (280 px against the vanilla 316 px ask).

sections.heading: NOT gate mask
sections.title: NOT gate mask
sections.description: A transpiler on `LogicGate.UpdateState` replaces the single `& 15` (four-bit mask) with `Mask` = `(1 << 31) - 1`, so a NOT gate with a ribbon input inverts all 31 bits. If the method has no such mask or more than one, it is left alone and a warning is logged.

sections.heading: OverlayLabelGuard
sections.title: OverlayLabelGuard
sections.description: When Better Automation Overlay (Workshop 1878896484) is enabled, prefixes every `GetSetting` on its `LogicLabelSetting` labels so a label that has not spawned yet returns blank text instead of throwing a NullReferenceException every frame. Applies even when the rest of the mod stands down.

sections.heading: OffsetGroups reach tables
sections.title: OffsetGroups reach tables
sections.description: The game keeps two tables of offsets that say where a duplicant may stand to work on a building. `InvertedStandardTable` reaches a diagonal cell only by way of one of its two orthogonal neighbours. `InvertedStandardTableWithCorners` reaches diagonal cells outright. The corner table is a strict superset of the standard one: every standing cell the standard table reaches, it reaches, by the same or a shorter row of intermediate cells.

sections.heading: Constructable.OnSpawn patch
sections.title: Constructable.OnSpawn patch
sections.description: Transpiler that replaces every `ldsfld OffsetGroups.InvertedStandardTable` in `Constructable.OnSpawn` with a load of the corner table. The game picks the corner table here for tiles only; after the patch every building gets it.

sections.heading: Deconstructable.OnSpawn patch
sections.title: Deconstructable.OnSpawn patch
sections.description: The same transpiler on `Deconstructable.OnSpawn`, so a building put up through a corner can be taken down through the same corner.

sections.heading: SwapTable
sections.title: SwapTable
sections.description: The shared instruction rewrite. Counts the swapped loads, logs `corner reach table in place` per method, or logs a warning and leaves the method unchanged when it no longer loads the standard table.

sections.heading: AnyElement
sections.title: AnyElement
sections.description: The Any choice. A `Tag` named `DetectAnyElement_Any`, created with the English name "Any" through `TagManager.Create`. It rides in the same saved `Filterable` field as element tags, so it is saved with the building and copied by copy-settings. Without the mod, a sensor saved on Any keeps the tag and matches nothing.

sections.heading: ModStrings
sections.title: ModStrings
sections.description: The mod's one string, `ModStrings.MISC.TAGS.DETECTANYELEMENT_ANY` ("Any"), registered under the game's `STRINGS.MISC.TAGS` and replaced from `translations/<locale>.po`. Chinese (Simplified), Korean and Russian ship; the template is `translations/DetectAnyElement.pot`.

sections.heading: FilterSideScreen.SetTarget patch
sections.title: FilterSideScreen.SetTarget patch
sections.description: Postfix that adds an Any row second in the list, under None, on screens with `isLogicFilter` (the pipe and rail element sensors and the in-world sensors; the conveyor and pipe filters keep only None). The row has its icon hidden, like None. The row is kept per screen in a `ConditionalWeakTable`, and selected when the target is already on Any.

sections.heading: ConduitElementSensor.ConduitUpdate patch
sections.title: ConduitElementSensor.ConduitUpdate patch
sections.description: Prefix for the Liquid Pipe, Gas Pipe and Conveyor Rail Element Sensors. On Any the sensor is on while the conduit at its cell holds mass above zero (any packet, whatever the element or item); it toggles the switch to match and skips the game's element test.

sections.heading: LogicElementSensor.Sim200ms patch
sections.title: LogicElementSensor.Sim200ms patch
sections.description: Prefix for the in-world Gas and Liquid Element Sensors. On Any the sensor is on while its cell holds any element of its desired state (any gas, or any liquid; vacuum counts as nothing). It keeps the game's eight-sample steadiness window (`samples`, `sampleIdx`) and drops only the element test.

sections.heading: LogicElementSensor.OnElementSelected patch
sections.title: LogicElementSensor.OnElementSelected patch
sections.description: Postfix that clears the "no element selected" status item when the choice is Any, since Any is a choice and not a lack of one.

sections.heading: AnyGlyph
sections.title: AnyGlyph
sections.description: `KMonoBehaviour` added to each of the five sensors. While the sensor is on Any it overrides the symbol `elements` (the icon the screen flashes when on) with an asterisk symbol from the mod's `detect_any_asterisk_kanim`, named `asterisk_<sensor kanim>`; each is in that icon's colour and offset to land mid-screen. Off or another choice removes the override. If the symbol is missing it logs a warning and the sensor keeps the vanilla icon.

sections.heading: SensorConfigs_DoPostConfigureComplete_Patch
sections.title: SensorConfigs_DoPostConfigureComplete_Patch
sections.description: Postfix on `DoPostConfigureComplete` of `LiquidConduitElementSensorConfig`, `GasConduitElementSensorConfig`, `SolidConduitElementSensorConfig`, `LogicElementSensorGasConfig` and `LogicElementSensorLiquidConfig`. Adds a `SymbolOverrideController` to the prefab when missing (it must exist before the anim controller is instantiated) and adds `AnyGlyph`.

sections.description: Delegate for the protected `Switch.Toggle`, which the sensors flip through.

documents.title: Jumper Bridges domain
documents.description: The classes, options, Harmony patches and saved state of Jumper Bridges (`JumperBridge`, `BridgeEndNode`, `BridgeKind`, `BridgeLinks`, `BridgeFootprint`), with the bridge end rules, key code paths and tests

sections.heading: JumperBridgesMod
sections.title: JumperBridgesMod
sections.description: The `UserMod2` entry point. Loads `Options` before `base.OnLoad` (which applies the patches) and sets each `BridgeKind.Enabled`, so a kind that is off has its patches skipped through `Prepare()`. Then initializes PLib, registers `ModStrings` with `Isochronous.Translations` and registers the options screen.

sections.heading: Options
sections.title: Options
sections.description: PLib options saved in the shared config location, both restart-required.

sections.heading: BridgeKind
sections.title: BridgeKind
sections.description: What differs between automation and power: the network manager, layers and wire art. Two instances, `Logic` and `Power`, in `BridgeKind.All`. Each keeps its own live node table, so an automation and a power bridge end on one cell are on two separate networks. `Of(BuildingDef)` maps `BuildLocationRule.LogicBridge` to Logic and `BuildLocationRule.WireBridge` to Power; the heavy-watt joint plates have their own rule and are left alone.

sections.heading: JumperBridge
sections.title: JumperBridge
sections.description: `KMonoBehaviour` on every complete bridge of an enabled kind. Gives each end that has no wire under it a `BridgeEndNode` (creation deferred a frame so a loaded save's wires have marked their cells first), removes the nodes when the bridge is deconstructed or broken (`BuildingBroken`) and recreates them on repair (`BuildingFullyRepaired`).

sections.heading: BridgeEndNode
sections.title: BridgeEndNode
sections.description: A `KAnimGraphTileVisualizer` on a standalone GameObject (no building) that stands in for a wire under a bridge end. It makes the three registrations a wire makes: the wire tile layer, a physical network node with connection bits and a network item at the cell, so the port there is told it is connected. It plays the wire kanim and mirrors the connection bits its neighbours point at it. Several bridge ends on one cell share one node, which goes with its last owner. It costs nothing, yields nothing, has no deconstruct order and is not saved. On a power network it is not a `Wire`, so the circuit's wattage limit is the bridge's own.

sections.heading: BridgeFootprint
sections.title: BridgeFootprint
sections.description: Registry of where every bridge is, by cell, on the complete and the under-construction prefab. The game puts a bridge on its end layer only at its two end cells and this mod stops a bridge taking that slot from a port or earlier bridge, so a bridge with both ends taken is on no layer. The deconstruct, cancel and prioritize tools find it here by its end cells.

sections.heading: BridgeLinks
sections.title: BridgeLinks
sections.description: Owns the network manager's link table for groups of bridges that share end cells. The manager keeps one link partner per cell, so after any bridge connects or disconnects, the distinct cells of its group are rewritten as a directed ring (c0 to c1 to ... to c0), sorted so the write is idempotent, then the networks are rebuilt.

sections.heading: Harmony patches
sections.title: Harmony patches
sections.description: The game classes and methods patched, grouped by purpose, all in `mods/jumper-bridges/src/JumperBridges/Patches.cs`. A group is skipped when its kind is off., Bridge setup (automation): `LogicWireBridgeConfig` and `LogicRibbonBridgeConfig` `DoPostConfigureComplete` and `DoPostConfigureUnderConstruction` add `JumperBridge` and `BridgeFootprint`., Bridge setup (power): `WireBridgeConfig` `DoPostConfigureComplete` and `DoPostConfigureUnderConstruction`., Placement: `BuildingDef.MarkArea`, `AreLogicPortsInValidPositions`, `IsValidWireBridgeLocation`, `IsValidHighWattBridgeLocation`, `ArePowerPortsInValidPositions`, `MarkOverlappingPorts`., Ports: `LogicPorts.CreatePhysicalPorts`, `DestroyPhysicalPorts`, `CreateVisualizers` (skipped for bridges)., Links: `LogicUtilityNetworkLink` and `WireUtilityNetworkLink` `OnConnect` and `OnDisconnect` call `BridgeLinks`., Wire art and drags: `KAnimGraphTileVisualizer.OnSpawn`, `UpdateConnections`, `OnCleanUp`; `BaseUtilityBuildTool.BuildPath`., Tools: `DisconnectTool.OnDragComplete` and `OnMouseMove`; `DeconstructTool.DeconstructCell`; `CancelTool.OnDragTool`; `PrioritizeTool.OnDragTool`., Overlays: `OverlayModes.Logic` and `OverlayModes.Power` `Update` and `Disable`.

sections.heading: FallPoke

sections.description: Static class with the whole mod. A postfix on `Pathfinding.AddNavGrid` subscribes to each navigation grid's `OnNavGridUpdateComplete`. A nested patch on `Door.SetWorldState` arms cells when a door finishes a state change. When a grid batch includes an armed cell, any critter standing in that cell whose navigation type is no longer valid there has `brain.UpdateBrain()` called, which runs normal chore selection and with it the game's fall check.

sections.title: Door_SetWorldState_Patch
sections.description: Postfix on `Door.SetWorldState`. Acts only when `updateSim` is true (the door's state machine entered open, closed or locked after the animation) and a scene is not loading. Arms the door's `PlacementCells`; with Critters Fall Through Open Doors present it also arms the cells below, above, left and right of each.

sections.heading: MultichannelCritterSensor (component)
sections.title: MultichannelCritterSensor (component)
sections.description: The building's behaviour. Every 200 ms (`ISim200ms`) it finds the room the building is in, counts creatures and eggs in the room cavity that pass the species filters, compares the totals against the thresholds, and sends the packed value through the ribbon port.

sections.heading: ThresholdAdapter
sections.title: ThresholdAdapter
sections.description: A small `MonoBehaviour` implementing the game's `IThresholdSwitch`, one per threshold (`Kind.Combined`, `Kind.Critters`, `Kind.Eggs`). It lets a cloned vanilla `ThresholdSwitchSideScreen` read and write one of the sensor's three thresholds. Setting a value clamps it to 0..64 and calls `NotifyConfigChanged`.

sections.heading: MultichannelCritterSensorSideScreen
sections.title: MultichannelCritterSensorSideScreen
sections.description: The side screen (`SideScreenContent`, `IRender200ms`). The frame is PLib UI; the three threshold editors are runtime clones of the vanilla `ThresholdSwitchSideScreen` prefab; the species and egg lists are clones of the storage-filter row and element prefabs (`TreeFilterableSideScreen`) driven directly. Layout: count line, mode buttons (Combined / Separate), combined editor, then a Critters section and an Eggs section, each with a count checkbox, an "All" row, a species list and (in separate mode) its own threshold editor.

sections.heading: CloneInToNewWorld_Patch
sections.title: CloneInToNewWorld_Patch
sections.description: The core patch, a postfix on `SettingsCache.CloneInToNewWorld`. `Apply` loads the options, calls `Plan` for every subworld, writes the resulting band tables into `MutatedWorldData.biomes.BiomeBackgroundElementBandConfigurations` and sets each chosen `SubWorld.backwallNoise`. Any exception is caught and logged and worldgen continues untouched. `Plan` decides without changing anything and is reused by the YAML export.

A `PatternGroup` is a subworld zone type (`SubWorld.ZoneType`) with a default pattern: Kelp for ToxicJungle, BoggyMarsh, Swamp, SugarWoods, PrehistoricGarden, PrehistoricWetlands; Abyss for OilField, Rust, MagmaCore, Barren, Wasteland, Metallic, Radioactive; Reef elsewhere; the Aquatic pack's own zones default to Vanilla.

sections.heading: UpgradeTool
sections.title: UpgradeTool
sections.description: The box-drag tool, a subclass of the game's `DragTool`. Cursor and area-visualizer assets are cloned from the vanilla Sweep (`ClearTool`) tool by reflection. Owns the dialog, the compiled plan, the highlight (blue for buildings the plan would touch, green for ones already pending), the overlay switch and the hover card. A drag works from the plan as it stood at the last Apply.

sections.heading: UpgradePlan, ChangeMaterialPlan, ReplaceTypePlan
sections.title: UpgradePlan, ChangeMaterialPlan, ReplaceTypePlan
sections.description: The player's choices on both tabs, kept for the session. `UpgradePlan.Current` holds the active `PlanMode` (`ChangeMaterial` or `ReplaceType`) and a `Version` bumped on every change, so highlights recompile. Each tab implements `IPlanTab` (`IsComplete`, `Summary`, `TouchedDefs`, `Compile`, `Save`, `Load`).

sections.heading: Matcher and Upgrade
sections.title: Matcher and Upgrade
sections.description: A plan compiled for a drag or highlight. `Matcher.Matches(building)` says whether the plan takes a building; `TryPlan(building, out Upgrade)` says what it becomes. `Upgrade` holds the target `BuildingDef`, the materials and `Rebuild` (deconstruct and reconstruct instead of building over). Made again when the plan changes and once a second, since research changes what is allowed.

sections.heading: Family and Category
sections.title: Family and Category
sections.description: A `Family` is a building type as the build menu lists it: usually one def, or several defs made by one config class when a mod makes one def per material and lists one (Decor Pack's stained glass tiles). A `Category` is a heading of families, by replacement layer or by build menu category.

sections.heading: Rules
sections.title: Rules
sections.description: `ReplacementRules` decides what the game lets be built over what (`IsReplaceable`, `CanReplace`, `IsBuildable`, source and target categories). `MaterialSwap` decides which types the Change material tab offers and which recipe ingredient a change swaps. `Materials` reads what a building was built from (`Deconstructable.constructionElements`). `Variants.Resolve` picks the def to build for a family and materials by running other mods' `BuildTool.Activate` prefixes.

sections.heading: Orders and PlacementQueue
sections.title: Orders and PlacementQueue
sections.description: `Orders.Place` queues one upgrade: `Replace` follows the build tool's sequence (`GetReplacementCandidate`, `IsReplacementLayerOccupied` over the footprint, `CanReplace`, same-type-same-material skip, `TryReplaceTile`, write into the replacement layer, priority from the tool menu); `Reconstruct` goes through `Reconstructable.RequestReconstruct` with every ingredient set. `PlacementQueue` places the drag's buildings in slices of about 4 ms a frame, re-checks each as placed, and shows the popup when the last is done. With instant build (debug toggle or sandbox setting) buildings are replaced on the spot.

sections.heading: Presets
sections.title: Presets
sections.description: A `PlanPreset` is one tab's plan saved by name, by prefab ID and element tag so it reads back in any colony. Each tab lists only its own presets and a name is unique within a tab. Stored in `mods/config/UpgradePlanner/presets.json` under the game's data folder (`Presets.FilePath`); tests point it elsewhere.

sections.heading: Window
sections.title: Window
sections.description: A PLib `PDialog` (`UpgradeDialog`), non-modal, with one view per tab (`MaterialTabView`, `TypeTabView`). Materials are picked in the game's own `MaterialSelectionPanel`, instantiated from the build menu's prefab (`MaterialPicker`). `Widgets.cs` holds shared controls, `ToolMarker` and `ToolIcon` the cursor marker and toolbar sprite, `PlannerHoverCard` the hover card.

sections.heading: Compat
sections.title: Compat
sections.description: `BlueprintsCompat` binds to Blueprints Expanded's `API_Methods.GetAllAdditionalBuildingData` and its `UnderConstructionDataTransfer` carrier, and sets `Loaded`. `OtherModSettings` registers Suppress Notifications' and No Manual Delivery's per-building settings with Blueprints Expanded's API. `ModCompat` patches Adaptive Building Menu's two layout appliers to skip the planner's pickers.

sections.heading: Hotkey

sections.heading: Insulated vent storage (patch on LiquidVentConfig)
sections.title: Insulated vent storage (patch on LiquidVentConfig)
sections.description: Gives each liquid vent's `Storage` the game's insulated storage modifiers (hide, seal, insulate), so the packet a vent is about to emit is skipped by the phase-transition handler and not temperature simulated. This prevents the tile inside the vent.

sections.heading: VentFreezeWatcher (component)
sections.title: VentFreezeWatcher (component)
sections.description: Added to every liquid vent. For the first second of running time after it spawns (five 200 ms ticks) it watches the vent cell and the landing cell, remembers what each held the previous tick, and asks the sim to dig a tile that could not have formed in normal play. Then it removes itself from the scheduler. Implements `ISim200ms`.

sections.heading: DigRequests
sections.title: DigRequests
sections.description: Static map of cells the watchers asked the sim to dig, and the patch that answers the sim's dig report for those cells by spawning the full mass as debris (a dug tile normally drops half). A request the sim ignores yields no report, so asking again is safe. Cleared on `Game.OnSpawn`.

sections.heading: DebugSave
sections.title: DebugSave
sections.description: Debug tooling. Reads the options once per game, logs vent emits in debug mode, and with the repro button arms a save that is written at the end of the frame in which a liquid vent next emits a packet, as `VentFreezeRepro.sav` next to the current save. That moment is the only one in which the bug's conditions can be captured.
